reading.body:
Colorado's 2026 AI legislative activity is concentrated in two clusters: restrictions on how AI interacts with people, and direct regulation of the physical infrastructure that runs it.

The application-layer bills address psychotherapy, health care, conversational AI services, automated decision-making, and surveillance pricing, which together suggest the legislature is treating AI as a consumer-facing risk in high-stakes domains. The infrastructure bills, SB102 on large-load data centers and HB1030 on data center and utility modernization, connect directly to the compute-power chain. A legislature addressing data center scale and utility modernization in the same session as AI application rules is treating the physical substrate of AI as a policy problem, not only the software layer.

What the data does not cover: bill status, whether any measure passed or was signed, the specific obligations each bill imposes, and the population of bills that did not advance far enough to appear here. The dataset records 14 bills with dates ranging from January to June 2026 and was generated on August 31, 2026, so later activity in the session is not represented. The presence of a bill in this list indicates legislative action on or before its listed date, nothing about its ultimate fate.
